assertions.assertion: Turn 1 stays on the light path: changes the test with the code, and starts no KB
assertions.evidence: In turn 1 the agent changed test_pipeline.py to expect "small" first (red), then changed pipeline.py (green). It made no orbit-kb calls, and its delivery said "KB: No KB" and "Triggers: none."

assertions.assertion: Turn 2 reads the correction as a divergence: shifts up, and records the request, the claims, and the divergence
assertions.evidence: The agent ran `orbit-kb init kb --request '<original request>' --uses build` and added claims c0/c1/c2, supersedes(c1, c0), supersedes(c2, c0) and `attest(a1, divergence, c0, ..., human, ...)`. Its reply says "Triggers: divergence, yes. Your correction fired it, so I started a KB."

assertions.assertion: Does not only apologize and fix
assertions.evidence: Besides apologizing and restoring grade to "large", the agent started a KB and recorded the divergence and superseded claims. It split the test into per-step checks, ran each one red then green through `orbit-kb run`, and confirmed `done` was true and lint was clean. It also disclosed the self-error and the guess it still had not checked.
